title: Securities Trading Policy
date_approved: Approved by the Board of WiseTech Global Limited; document dated 16 October 2021

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: All Directors of the Company and all Group employees, collectively defined as Employees. Subject to the insider trading prohibition, any Company-imposed dealing notice, the six month short-term and speculative dealing ban and the hedging restrictions on unvested and locked plan securities. No blackout period, notification or approval requirement applies to this tier.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Directors; the senior management team as defined by the CEO from time to time; and other persons who regularly possess inside information and who have been advised by the Company Secretary that they are subject to special restrictions. Subject to the blackout periods, the notification or approval regime and the margin lending approval requirement. Must also take steps in relation to dealings by persons over whom they have, or are deemed to have, investment control or influence.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of the Company. Restricted Persons who, uniquely, need only notify rather than obtain approval before dealing outside a blackout period, and who must confirm each trade to the Company Secretary afterwards.

tiers.name: other key management personnel
tiers.description: Key management personnel other than Directors; distinguished only by the post-trade confirmation obligation in section 5.7, which they share with Directors.

tiers.name: persons over whom they have, or are deemed to have, investment control or influence
tiers.description: Persons whose dealings a Restricted Person controls or influences, or is deemed to control or influence. The policy does not define the class further; the Restricted Person must take steps in relation to their dealings.

definitions.hedging_definition: Hedging is entering into any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding the Company's securities.

windows.start_anchor: close of trading on the ASX on 30 June each year
windows.end_anchor: the day of the announcement to ASX of the full-year results (inclusive)

windows.start_anchor: close of trading on the ASX on 31 December each year
windows.end_anchor: the day of the announcement to ASX of the half-year results (inclusive)

windows.start_anchor: any other period that the Board specifies from time to time

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: Two separate powers. The Board may specify 'any other period' as a blackout period for Restricted Persons under section 5.1. Separately, under section 4.1 the Company may notify Employees generally that they must not deal, either for a specified period or until the Company gives further notice. Neither power is stated to be confidential, but a refused or revoked approval must be kept confidential by the applicant.

rules.detail: Absolute ban with no clearance route and no exceptional-circumstances relief, applying to every Employee and not just Restricted Persons. Confined to securities acquired under an employee or director equity plan operated by the Company.
rules.evidence: Company securities acquired under an employee or director equity plan operated by the Company must never be hedged prior to vesting.

rules.detail: Vested plan securities remain unhedgeable for as long as a holding lock or plan dealing restriction subsists. The word 'never' rules out approval.
rules.evidence: Company securities must never be hedged while they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of an employee or director equity plan operated by the Company.

rules.detail: Section 4.3 defines hedging broadly but restricts it in only two states: pre-vesting, and while a holding lock or plan restriction applies. Hedging vested, unrestricted securities, including shares bought on market, is not prohibited. This is the key permissive feature of the policy, subject to the substance over form principle in section 1 and to the notification or approval overlay if the arrangement is characterised as a dealing.
rules.evidence: Hedging is entering into any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding the Company's securities.

rules.detail: There is no derivatives clause and no definition of 'the Company's securities'. If the OTC put and call are treated as a dealing in the Company's securities, a Director need only notify the Company Secretary and the Chair (or the Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee in the Chair's own case) before dealing, may then deal for 5 business days, and must confirm the trade afterwards. No approval is required and no reason can be refused.
rules.evidence: During any period that is not a trading blackout period under section 5.1, Directors must, prior to any proposed dealing, provide notification of the proposed dealing in the Company's securities to the Company Secretary and: 1) the Chair of the Board (in the case of other Directors); or 2) the Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee (in the case of the Chair of the Board).

rules.detail: Restricted Persons other than Directors must obtain approval on a Clearance to Trade Request Form, answered typically within one business day, with the approver free to refuse without reasons, impose conditions or revoke at any time; the approved dealing should occur within 5 business days.
rules.evidence: During any period that is not a trading blackout period under section 5.1, Restricted Persons other than Directors must, prior to any proposed dealing, seek approval for the proposed dealing in the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Blackout periods, notification and approval apply only to Restricted Persons. An Employee outside that group faces only the insider trading prohibition, the short-term and speculative dealing bans and the hedging restrictions on unvested and locked plan securities.
rules.evidence: Certain parts of this Policy apply only to Restricted Persons

rules.detail: Forward contracts are the policy's own example of a short term dealing, so a forward monetisation maturing within six months is prohibited outright. A longer-dated prepaid forward or forward sale is not banned and, for a Restricted Person, would be a dealing requiring notification (Directors) or approval (other Restricted Persons).
rules.evidence: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 6 month period, and entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts).

rules.detail: Named as an instance of speculative dealing and banned for all Employees, with the borrow-and-sell mechanic spelled out. No approval route.
rules.evidence: Employees must not deal in the Company's securities on a speculative basis, including short selling. Short selling involves borrowing and selling securities in the hope that they can be bought back at a lower price in the future to close out the short position at a profit.

rules.detail: Lending out one's own Company securities is not addressed. Securities borrowing appears only in the descriptive definition of short selling.

Contracts for difference are not named. A CFD over Company securities would ordinarily be a speculative dealing and, if closed within six months, also short-term trading, so it is caught by the section 4.2 bans rather than by any express clause.
rules.evidence: Employees must not deal in the Company's securities on a speculative basis, including short selling.

rules.detail: Margin lending is permitted with approval under the section 5.5 process, and the Company may make approval conditional on any terms it sees fit, the stated example being the circumstances in which securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call. Transferring existing Company securities into an existing margin loan account is a separate approval trigger. No vesting restriction on the collateral is imposed.
rules.evidence: Approval must be obtained in accordance with the procedure set out in section 5.5 for any: 1) entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of the Company's securities; and 2) transferring securities in the Company into an existing margin loan account.

rules.detail: Section 5.6 sits in Part 5, headed 'Additional restrictions applying to Restricted Persons', so an Employee who is not a Restricted Person needs no approval for a margin loan over Company securities.

Granting a charge, mortgage, pledge or lien over Company securities is not mentioned anywhere, is not within the description of dealing in section 3, and is not a listed approval trigger. Only margin lending arrangements are named.

Secured financing generally is not named; only 'a margin lending arrangement in respect of the Company's securities' is. A bank loan secured on collared shares is not a margin loan in the retail sense, but given the substance over form principle it should be treated as within section 5.6 and cleared, and no prohibition applies either way. Nothing in the policy bans secured financing over Company securities.
rules.evidence: entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of the Company's securities

rules.detail: Six month buy-sell window, extended beyond on-market trades to 'other short term dealings', with forward contracts given as the example. Selling shares received on vesting under an employee or director equity plan within 6 months of vesting is carved out. The ban does not apply to Excluded Dealings under section 6.
rules.evidence: Selling shares received on vesting of entitlements under an employee or director equity plan within 6 months of the vesting date is not short-term trading.

clearance.approver: Company Secretary and the Chair of the Board; the Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee in the case of the Chair of the Board
clearance.post_trade_deadline: promptly, ideally by close of business on the day the trade is entered into
clearance.evidence: Subject always to the insider trading prohibition in the Corporations Act, a Director may deal at any time for a period of 5 business days following notification. By notifying their intention to deal, the Director is taken to have satisfied themselves that the proposed dealing is within the terms of this Securities Trading Policy.

clearance.approver: Company Secretary (Clearance to Trade Request Form); the approver may consult members of management as appropriate
clearance.post_trade_deadline: promptly, ideally by close of business on the day the trade is entered into
clearance.evidence: A request for approval to deal will be answered as soon as practicable and typically within one business day. ... The approver is not obliged to provide reasons for any aspect of their decision, and may revoke their approval at any time. If a request is not approved or an approval is revoked, that fact must be kept confidential.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: promptly, ideally by close of business on the day the trade is entered into
clearance.evidence: Following any trade, Directors and other key management personnel must promptly notify the Company Secretary, ideally by close of business on the day the trade is entered into. This is to assist the Company to comply with its disclosure obligations.
Certain parts of this Policy apply only to Restricted Persons

short_term.basis: buying and selling securities on market within a 6 month period, and entering into other short term dealings
carve_outs: Selling shares received on vesting of entitlements under an employee or director equity plan within 6 months of the vesting date

the Excluded Dealings listed in section 6, including participation in an employee or director equity plan, dividend reinvestment plan, share purchase plan, rights issue, acceptance of a takeover, dealings with no effective change in beneficial interest, pre-approved non-discretionary trading plans, and a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights
short_term.evidence: Employees must not deal in the Company's securities on a short-term trading basis. Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 6 month period, and entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts).

exceptions.evidence: a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.

exceptions.approver: The approver under the section 5.5 written request process (Clearance to Trade Request Form submitted to the Company Secretary)
exceptions.evidence: If a Restricted Person needs to deal in securities during a blackout period due to exceptional circumstances and is not in possession of any inside information, then, they may apply for approval to deal. Exceptional circumstances are likely to include severe financial hardship or compulsion by court order.

exceptions.approver: The approver under the section 5.5 written request process
exceptions.evidence: Exceptional circumstances are likely to include severe financial hardship or compulsion by court order.

participation in an employee or director equity plan operated by the Company. However, where securities in the Company granted under an employee or director equity plan cease to be held under the terms of that plan, any dealings in those securities must only occur in accordance with this Policy

acquisition of Company securities through a dividend reinvestment plan; acquisition of Company securities through a share purchase plan available to all retail shareholders; acquisition of Company securities through a rights issue
the disposal of Company securities through the acceptance of a takeover offer, scheme of arrangement or equal access buy-back

dealings that result in no effective change to the beneficial interest in the securities (for example, transfers of Company securities already held into a superannuation fund or trust of which the Employee is a beneficiary)

trading under a pre-approved non-discretionary trading plan, where the Employee did not enter into the plan or amend the plan during a blackout period, the plan does not permit the Employee to exercise any influence or discretion in relation to trading under the plan and the plan cannot be cancelled during a blackout period, other than in exceptional circumstances

financing.price_trigger_guidance: No price triggers are prescribed, but section 5.6(b) gives the Company an open-ended power to condition a margin lending approval, with the stated example being 'the circumstances in which the Company's securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call'. In practice the loan-to-value ratio, margin call mechanics and any standstill in a blackout period are matters the Company Secretary can dictate as a condition of approval.

external_documents: The list of the senior management team as defined by the CEO from time to time
Terms of the Company's employee and director equity plans (holding locks and restrictions on dealing)
exemption_authority: The approver under the section 5.5 written request process (requests submitted to the Company Secretary) may grant approval for a Restricted Person to deal during a blackout period in exceptional circumstances, likely to include severe financial hardship or compulsion by court order, where the application is accompanied by sufficient evidence that the dealing is the most reasonable course of action available. The approver may refuse without reasons, impose conditions and revoke at any time. There is no authority to waive the section 4.3 hedging bans on unvested or locked securities, which are expressed as 'must never'.
jurisdiction_overlays: ASX Listing Rule 12.10 and the Company's ASX disclosure obligations for director and KMP trades

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban limited to unvested and locked securities
bespoke_clauses.clause: Company securities acquired under an employee or director equity plan operated by the Company must never be hedged prior to vesting. Company securities must never be hedged while they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of an employee or director equity plan operated by the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The hedging section is drafted as two targeted prohibitions rather than a general ban, so hedging vested unrestricted shares is left permitted and the derivative legs of a collar over those shares are available.

bespoke_clauses.topic: secured lender enforcement is an excluded dealing
bespoke_clauses.clause: Sections 4.2, 5.1, 5.3 and 5.4 of this Policy do not apply to ... a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the most bank-friendly clause in the policy: enforcement by the lender, even in a blackout period, is expressly carved out of the short-term trading ban, the blackout and the notification and approval requirements, so the executive is not put in breach by the bank's own sale.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company may, at its discretion, make any approval granted in accordance with section 5.6(a) conditional upon such terms and conditions as the Company sees fit (for example, with regard to the circumstances in which the Company's securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Company can dictate the enforcement mechanics of the facility as a condition of approving it, so the bank should expect the loan documentation to be negotiated with the Company Secretary rather than approved as presented.

bespoke_clauses.topic: directors notify rather than seek approval
bespoke_clauses.clause: a Director may deal at any time for a period of 5 business days following notification. By notifying their intention to deal, the Director is taken to have satisfied themselves that the proposed dealing is within the terms of this Securities Trading Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Directors self-certify for ordinary dealings, giving a clean 5 business day execution window with no approval risk; note that this route does not extend to margin lending, which needs approval under section 5.6 regardless of tier.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar that in substance hedges unvested or locked plan securities, even if written over an equal number of unrestricted shares, would be treated as breaching section 4.3, and a bespoke loan secured on shares should be cleared as if it were a margin lending arrangement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy names only 'a margin lending arrangement in respect of the Company's securities' and 'transferring securities in the Company into an existing margin loan account' as financing triggers.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no general prohibition on granting security over Company securities and no financier disclosure regime, so the funding leg of a collar is unobstructed on the face of the policy.

bespoke_clauses.topic: forward contracts as short term dealings
bespoke_clauses.clause: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 6 month period, and entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The tenor of the collar and of any forward element must exceed six months, and the collared shares should not have been bought on market within the preceding six months.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees must not deal in the Company's securities if ... the Company has notified Employees that they must not deal in securities (either for a specified period, or until the Company gives further notice).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An open-ended notice can be issued to all Employees at any time and would block collar entry, unwind or physical settlement without any stated end date.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy refers throughout to 'the Company's securities' without defining the term and contains no derivatives or securities definition.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: It is arguable that a bank-written OTC option is not itself one of 'the Company's securities', so the notification and approval regime may not formally bite on the derivative legs; the prudent course is to notify or clear them anyway given the substance over form clause.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A request for approval to deal will be answered as soon as practicable and typically within one business day.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An unusually fast and explicit service level, which makes it practical to align clearance with pricing on a specific trade date.

summary: A funded collar is realistically achievable at WiseTech, which is one of the more permissive policies in the market. Hedging is banned only for plan securities that are unvested or subject to a holding lock or plan dealing restriction, so vested unrestricted shares, including shares bought on market, may be hedged; the derivative legs would be a dealing requiring only prior notification to the Company Secretary and the Chair for a Director (with a 5 business day window and a same-day post-trade confirmation), or approval on a Clearance to Trade Request Form for other Restricted Persons, answered typically within one business day. The funding leg is likewise available: the only financing rule is that a margin lending arrangement, or a transfer of shares into an existing margin loan account, needs approval under section 5.5, and the Company may impose conditions on that approval, notably about when shares may be sold to satisfy a margin call; there is no encumbrance ban, no vesting restriction on collateral and no financier disclosure obligation. Critically, section 6(e) treats a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights as an Excluded Dealing outside the short-term trading ban, the blackout periods and the notification and approval requirements, so a bank enforcement sale does not put the executive in breach. The practical conditions are that entry falls outside the 30 June and 31 December blackout periods and any Board-specified or Company-notified dealing ban, that the tenor and the seasoning of the underlying shares both exceed six months to avoid the short-term dealing rule, and that the structure is disclosed and cleared on a substance over form basis, since the Company can condition its approval on the enforcement mechanics of the loan.
